submission.justification: Selection-S2 (gradient-boosted classifier) gives the highest expected significance in the statistical-only Monte Carlo study. At 55% signal efficiency it reaches 4.12 sigma, against 3.3 sigma for S1 and 2.6 sigma for S3 at 50%. S2 scans over 40-55% efficiency give a flat plateau at about 4.09-4.12 sigma, falling to about 4.0 sigma at 60% and 70% and to 3.85 sigma at 30%. Within that plateau, 55% gave the highest measured value, though the differences between 40%, 50% and 55% are within MC noise. S2 also stays the best strategy at every working point tested, and it matches the 2025 summary (4.1 sigma at 50%). The working point (55%) lies inside the 20-80% allowed range. The trigger is fully efficient above 30 GeV for all strategies, so it does not discriminate between them. Caveat on background robustness: the tool reports statistical uncertainty only, and no document quantifies systematic uncertainties on the background for any strategy. S2 uses jet substructure, which can carry larger modelling systematics than the kinematic-only S1, so the robustness requirement is not verified here. Before unblinding, the background estimate should be checked against data-driven control regions and systematic variations for S2, and S1 should be kept as a fallback if those checks fail.
